issues.failure_explanation: The statement defines $\sigma_k$ as distinct neglected singular values with multiplicities $m_k$, but the displayed sum is $\sum_k \sigma_k$, i.e. each distinct value is counted once. For a repeated neglected singular value, the standard balanced-truncation error contribution is its multiplicity times the singular value; counting it once gives a materially smaller and generally false bound.

failure_location.quote: bounded by twice the sum of the neglected singular values, multiplicities not counted, times the $L_2$ norm of the input function

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the sum by the multiplicity-weighted sum $\sum_k m_k\sigma_k$, or provide a self-contained proof that multiplicities can be omitted.
issues.overall_effect: The classical SLS error estimate stated by the paper is unreliable whenever neglected Hankel singular values have multiplicity greater than one, including the limiting single-mode LTI case.
issues.title: Balanced-truncation bound counts non-simple singular values only once
issues.why_classification: A source-supported repair is a contained weakening to the standard multiplicity-weighted bound; the advertised sharper distinct-value form is lost, but a comparable error guarantee survives.

issues.failure_explanation: The operator $\calL$ is the Kronecker-sum Lyapunov operator. Its smallest singular value is not generally $2\sigma_{\min}(A)$. For example, if $A=-aI+bJ$ with $J=J^T=-J$ and $b\gg a>0$, then $A$ is normal and Hurwitz, $\sigma_{\min}(A)=\sqrt{a^2+b^2}$, while $\sigma_{\min}(\calL)=2a$. The stated bound can therefore be violated by an arbitrarily large factor.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace $2\sigma_{\min}(A)$ by a valid bound on $\|\calL^{-1}\|$ or $\sigma_{\min}(\calL)$, and re-derive the stopping criterion with that constant.
issues.overall_effect: The certified error-residual relation for approximate Lyapunov solves is false, and the main GLE error bound depending on it is unreliable as stated.
issues.title: Lyapunov error-residual constant uses false singular-value identity
issues.why_classification: The formal error-bound structure survives with a correct operator-norm constant, but the specific efficiently computable constant advertised in the source is false and must be replaced.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof drops the factor $\fU_{k-1}^\T$ from $\|(\fZ_k-\fZ_{k-1})\fSigma_{k-1}^{1/2}\fU_{k-1}^\T\|_F$ and replaces it by $\|(\fZ_k-\fZ_{k-1})\fSigma_{k-1}^{1/2}\|_F$. Right multiplication by an orthonormal row factor is not an isometry in general. A concrete $2\times2$ factor example with $\fZ_{k-1}=[[0,0],[1,0]]$ and $\fZ_k=[[0.1,10],[1,0]]$ gives a true Frobenius difference far larger than the claimed right-hand side.

failure_location.quote: we used the fact that $\fU_k$ and $\fU_{k-1}$ have orthonormal columns

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Revise the inequality to keep the correct orthonormal factor, or replace it with a valid upper bound such as one using $\|\fU_{k-1}^\T\|_2=1$ and the singular values of $\fSigma_{k-1}^{1/2}$, then update the theorem and stopping criterion accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The computable quantity $\Delta_{k,k-1}$ can underestimate $\|\fX_k-\fX_{k-1}\|_F$, so the certified GLE error bound and stopping criterion can fail to guarantee the requested tolerance.
issues.title: Frobenius difference bound incorrectly drops orthonormal factor
issues.why_classification: A valid difference bound can replace the displayed one without changing the overall architecture, but the specific efficient bound used in the main certification is false and must be corrected.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof bounds $\fw^\T\fA_j^\T\fw$ below in magnitude by $\sigma_{\min}(\fA_j)\|\fw\|_2^2$. Dissipativity only gives $\fw^\T\fA_j\fw<0$, not this singular-value bound. For $\fA_j=-aI+bJ$ with $J^T=-J$ and $b\gg a>0$, $\fw^\T\fA_j^\T\fw=-a\|\fw\|_2^2$, while $\sigma_{\min}(\fA_j)\approx b$, so the claimed bound fails and the chosen $\perturbation$ need not make the LMI hold.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, replace the spectral condition number by a valid lower bound on the symmetric dissipation (e.g. the smallest eigenvalue of $-(\fA_j+\fA_j^T)/2$) and re-derive the required $\perturbation$, or impose that stronger condition explicitly.
issues.overall_effect: The guarantee that the perturbed approximate Gramian $\hat{\fX}=\tilde{\fX}+\perturbation I$ satisfies the stability LMI is false for the stated class, undermining the paper's claimed way to recover stability and error certification from approximate GLE solutions.
issues.title: Perturbation theorem uses an invalid lower bound for dissipative matrices
issues.why_classification: The advertised stability-recovery guarantee for the stated dissipative class does not survive; a repair necessarily changes the quantitative hypothesis and perturbation size.
